$comment: PROPOSED. pAI-OS does not publish an ability manifest schema we could
find, so the field names here are ours and are meant to be replaced by
theirs. What matters for review is not the spelling but the four things
an ability of this kind needs from its host — see `requires` below, and
kwaai/README.md for what each one means and why.
name: Owner authority
summary: Decide what other people's agents may do with your accounts, on your device.
description: Holds your authorization policy and answers on your behalf when somebody
else's AI agent asks for access to something of yours. The agent
negotiates against your terms, signs them, and gets a grant bound to one
operation — or waits while this ability asks you.
This is not an agent and it does not act for you. It is the thing that

key.why: Every request this ability makes to the authority is signed with a key that is yours. It is the whole credential — there is no account and no token.
key.needs: an Ed25519 signing key the host holds and will sign bytes with, and which does not leave the device

presence.why: Requests arrive when you are not looking at them. Somebody has to be asked.
presence.needs: a way to put a question in front of the person and get back approve or deny, with an unbounded wait

network.why: The authority is reachable over http on the device, or wherever the person put it.
network.needs: outbound http to a configured base URL

storage.why: Her policy and her ledger outlive a restart.
storage.needs: a durable place for the authority's own state

provides.summary: Answers whether another party's agent may touch this person's resources.

authority_url.summary: Her authorization server. Runs alongside this ability.

authority_name.summary: The authority the request signature is reconstructed against. Configuration on both sides, never read off the request.

auto_approve_tiers.summary: Tiers to answer without asking. Empty by default: an ability that answers for her by default is not doing the job.
